item.title: The law of the gravity well: why comfort kills talent
item.description:
We tend to think that if parents achieve a great deal, their children will automatically inherit their success. Life often shows the opposite: children of rich and famous parents often remain in the shadows, while people from poor families become titans of industry. The USA system explains this through rigorous physics, the laws of topology and energy balance, rather than mysticism.

Inheritance is a map, not a route

Successful parents create around their family what we call a Channel or a “gravity well.” They have laid out a path and accumulated experience and knowledge. The child is born into protected conditions rather than a vacuum, with substantial starting resources: access to money, education, and connections. It is like being given a map to a vein of gold. But the map is not gold. This is where the main law comes in, the law of finitude, or the limited nature of resources.

item.title: What falls outside axiomatics: meaning, value, and the other person
item.description:
The USA system describes action through rigorous mechanisms: a state, a transition, the extraction of structure, a rule change, and an observation. These five objects suffice to describe any action as a process. But three things do not fit this scheme.

Meaning, value, and the other person. This does not mean the system is wrong. It means the system has a boundary, and it is important to understand where that boundary lies. This article examines what remains outside axiomatics and why this is a property of the system rather than a flaw.
